injections.original_text: SHAP values are based on game theory
injections.injected_text: SHAP values are based on information theory
injections.rationale: Drifts the methodological basis attributed to the SHAP citation from game theory to information theory. SHAP is explicitly built on Shapley values from cooperative game theory — the cited paper is 'A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions' and the acronym itself expands to SHapley Additive exPlanations — so the injected basis mis-describes the cited method. Cite key untouched; two existing words perturbed.
injections.ground_truth_description: SHAP citation: theoretical basis changed from 'game theory' to 'information theory', mis-describing the cited method's foundation.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) \cite{lundberg2017unified}: SHAP values are based on game theory and provide a unified measure of feature importance for individual predictions.

The table occurrence is shifted by one order of magnitude to 4.6730 while the prose retains 0.4673, so the same measurement disagrees by 10x between the two statements. The injected value is additionally outside the [0,1] range a fidelity score can take.
injections.ground_truth_description: Results table: LIME fidelity changed 0.4673 -> 4.6730 (x10), contradicting the 0.4673 restated in the prose and exceeding the valid [0,1] range for fidelity.

injections.original_text: \item Counterfactual Explanations \cite{arrieta2020explainable}: Counterfactual explanations provide insights into the model's decision-making process by identifying the minimal changes required in the input data to achieve a different prediction outcome.
injections.injected_text: \item Counterfactual Explanations \cite{arrieta2020explainable}: Counterfactual explanations provide insights into the model's decision-making process by identifying the minimal changes required in the input data to achieve the same prediction outcome.
injections.rationale: Swapping 'different' for 'same' reverses the cited definition of a counterfactual explanation, directly contradicting the mathematical mechanism detailed in Arrieta et al. (2020).
injections.ground_truth_description: Reversed the outcome of counterfactual explanations from achieving a different prediction to achieving the same prediction.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: Counterfactual Explanations \cite{arrieta2020explainable}: Counterfactual explanations provide insights into the model's decision-making process by identifying the minimal changes required in the input data to achieve a different prediction outcome.

injections.rationale: Inverts the Fidelity ratio so the residual norm becomes the denominator. The form is structurally similar but wrong: the metric is defined as a normalised residual that goes to 0 as the surrogate g approaches the model f, whereas the inverted form diverges in that limit — contradicting the paper's own reading of low fidelity values as good agreement. Perturbs the existing equation in place rather than appending a claim.
injections.ground_truth_description: Fidelity definition: ratio inverted from ||f-g||^2 / ||f||^2 to ||f||^2 / ||f-g||^2, so the metric diverges instead of vanishing under perfect surrogate agreement.

truth.term_role: normalised-residual ratio in the fidelity metric
